content.text: {"label":"system_slowness","explanation":"Call volumes are on forecast in both queues (today -2.1% payments, -2.5% general), and no call reason stands out apart from a mild rise in refund_status. Attendance is normal, with 2 sick per queue against a usual 2.4-2.6. Handle time, however, is up sharply on both queues (+39% payments, +58% general). This matches open P2 incident INC-20261021-5862, where CRM customer search is taking 20-40 s and slowing every call. Service level fell to 35% on payments and 52% on general at 12:45, as the morning mitigations ended at 13:00.","plan_name":"CRM slowness: renew mitigations and add overtime for the afternoon","rationale":"The slowness inflates workload on both queues, so neither can donate agents and cross-skilling is ruled out. There is no customer-facing outage, so an outage message is not appropriate. All the morning levers ended at or before 13:00, so I renew the free and cheap ones. I delay lunch breaks 13:00-14:30 by 30 min; agents already delayed this morning are skipped. Coaching is cancelled for the rest of the day, IVR callback is restored to shave peaks, and 20% of eligible enquiries are deflected to chat. For real added capacity, I make fresh overtime offers covering 13:30-17:30. The morning offers used about Rs 5,760 (around 8 accepted agents x 2 h). The new offers add roughly Rs 7,200 (about 10 accepted agents x 2 h), keeping the day near Rs 13,000, under the Rs 15,000 budget. These measures should be reviewed once CRM is
